subject: SentinelSys on-prem throughput degradation & exec sync
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@sentinelsys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: SentinelSys Infra <infra@sentinelsys.com>
Date: 2028-08-12T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p95 latency and 5xx spike on our on-prem cluster

Hi Vivek / Marissa —

We started seeing a large regression in tail latency and a burst of 5xx errors on our private on-prem deployment this morning (~08:00 PST). P95 has moved from ~220ms to 1.9s and overall success rate dropped to ~87% on our production route. Attached is a short set of perf graphs and a sample error log.

This is customer-impacting (billing flows and search). Can Redwood please: 
- confirm triage steps you will run now,
- open a bridge (we can join), and
- let us know any immediate mitigations (model fallback, reduced concurrency)

Alex
Alex Monroe
Head of Infra Eng, SentinelSys
Attachments: perf-graphs-08-12.png
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@sentinelsys.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-12T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency and 5xx spike on our on-prem cluster

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the graphs. I've started a triage and opened a temporary bridge (details below). We're treating this as high-priority. Immediate items we are running now: 

1) Confirm whether this is compute or IO constrained (collecting top / iostat / nvme stats).
2) Check KV cache pressure and prefix cache hit rates; if cache eviction is high, we'll temporarily reduce concurrency.
3) Validate runtime kernel params and swap activity.
4) If necessary: failover to a smaller model variant and disable batching for critical routes.

Diego, can you gather heap dumps and NVMe metrics from the three nodes that show the worst latency? Marissa, please confirm whether Sentinel wants an exec-level sync (CTO) if we recommend a rolling maintenance window.

Bridge: redwood.redact/bridge/INC-7791 (on-call link)
On-call: diego_fernandez@redwood.com

– Vivek
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@sentinelsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency and 5xx spike on our on-prem cluster

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed: CPU steal on node node-13 (high iowait); NVMe write latency spiking correlated with the period of increased p95.
- Runtime: kernel was recently bumped to 6.5.x by customer ops; /proc/sys/vm/overcommit_memory is set to 0 (we prefer 1 for our runtime).
- KV cache: eviction rate up ~38% last 30m; prefix cache hit ratio fell from 0.82 -> 0.56.

Actions taken (11:00–11:30):
- Collected heap snapshot (node-13): node-heapdump-08-13.txt.gz (attached).
- Temporarily reduced max concurrency for prod route to 50% (fall-through to retry path enabled).
- Increased runtime log level for decode and cache eviction events for 1h.

Next steps:
- Suggest immediate kernel tuning (vm.overcommit_memory=1) and NVMe driver param review with customer infra.
- If storage latency continues, we should schedule a rolling restart of the serving pool with a faster checkpoint strategy (prune KV cache aggressively before restart).

I'll remain on the bridge and can run the restart if we get sign-off.

— Diego
SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: node-heapdump-08-13.txt.gz
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@sentinelsys.com>; Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@sentinelsys.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-12T12:14:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p95 latency and 5xx spike on our on-prem cluster

Priya / Alex —

We're on this and have initiated mitigation steps. SentinelOps has been looped for kernel param changes. Vivek's team will propose a short maintenance window if needed; I want to confirm expectations from your side about availability and customer notification.

I created a mutual action plan to capture the technical and commercial impacts so we can escalate with internal leadership if outage risk continues: https://drive.google.com/sentinelsys/MAP-7791 (attached as PDF).

If this moves to an extended maintenance, please note our standard practice is to offer service credits proportionate to downtime — we'll coordinate with finance if that becomes necessary. For now, can we confirm a 4-hour rolling restart window (off-peak 02:00–06:00 PST) as a contingency?

Thanks,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: mutual-action-plan-sentinelsys.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-13T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief: SentinelSys on-prem performance regression (recommended remediation)

Grace / Karthik —

Summary: SentinelSys (private on-prem cluster) experienced a sudden regression in p95 latency and error rate starting 2028-08-12 08:00 PST. Our triage indicates storage IO pressure on a subset of nodes combined with aggressive KV cache eviction leading to higher decode overhead and retries. Customer impact: critical flows (billing + search) degraded; estimated ~13% revenue risk while issue persists.

Proposed remediation (short term):
- Apply vm.overcommit_memory=1 on the affected nodes (low risk; requires sudo).
- Adjust NVMe scheduler param to reduce write amplification (cust infra approval).
- Temporarily reduce batch sizes and concurrency on affected routes (already applied).
- Prune KV cache before a rolling restart of the runtime to avoid cold-cache storm.

Operational ask: Need executive approval to schedule a 4-hour rolling maintenance window (02:00–06:00 PST next maintenance night). Diego and one Redwood on-call engineer will be present on bridge. Customer has requested Redwood on-call during maintenance.

If you approve, we'll send a formal change notice to SentinelOps and schedule a pilot restart on a single node tonight.

– Vivek
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Singh <psingh@sentinelsys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@sentinelsys.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec brief: SentinelSys on-prem performance regression (recommended remediation)

Vivek / Marissa — thank you for the clear triage and plan. We agree to the proposed 4-hour rolling maintenance (start window: 02:00 PST next night) provided: 

1) Redwood places a named on-call engineer on the bridge for the duration (Diego is fine).
2) We get a one-hour planned blackout notice to customers (we will take customer-facing ownership of notification).
3) Redwood confirms rollback steps and a post-mortem timeline (within 72 hours).

Please proceed with the pilot restart tonight on a non-prod node and share the results. We'll be on the maint bridge for the scheduled window.

Regards,
Priya Singh
CTO, SentinelSys
